# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 32 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_032_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 4, Chapter 2 — Post-Baptismal Repentance

**1** I asked him again and said, "Sir, I heard from some teachers that there is no other repentance except the one given at baptism, when we went down into the water and received forgiveness of our former sins." **2** He said to me: "You have heard correctly, for that is so. For the one who has received forgiveness of sins ought no more to sin, but to dwell in purity. **3** Since, however, you ask diligently about all things, I will show you this also — not giving an occasion for error to those who are about to believe or who have recently believed in the Lord. For those who have recently believed and those who are about to believe have no repentance of sins; they have a remission of their former sins. **4** For those who were called before these days — for them the Lord established repentance. For the Lord, knowing the heart and knowing all things beforehand, knew the weakness of men and the many wiles of the devil, that he would do some mischief to the servants of God and would deal wickedly with them. **5** Therefore, in his great mercy the Lord had compassion on his creation and established this one repentance, and to me was given authority over this repentance. **6** But I tell you," he said, "if after this great and holy calling any one, being tempted by the devil, commits sin, he has only one repentance. But if he sins and repents repeatedly, it is of no profit to such a man; for he will have difficulty in living to God." **7** I said to him, "I received life when I heard these things so carefully from you; for I know that if I do not add to my sins any more, I shall be saved." He replied, "You will be saved — you and all whoever do these things."

---

*EMET note: Chapter 32 is THE most discussed passage in the entire Shepherd, and one of the most historically significant texts in early Christian theology. The issue: is there post-baptismal repentance? The Shepherd's answer: YES — one time only, as a unique divine provision for the weakness of the flesh. This directly contradicts stricter views (Tertullian, Novatian) and is more liberal than the Hebrews 6:4-6 position. The Shepherd's position became the dominant Catholic tradition.*
